Subject: Spike of 503/504 + 429s across EU/APAC — urgent

Hi Kimberly / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained wave of 503/504 responses for a subset of our checkout traffic originating from EU regions starting ~08:45 UTC. At the same time, our front end shows an uptick in 429s that looks like client-side retry amplification. Impact: ~12% failure rate on payment tokenization calls (affecting ~18% of transactions for EU customers) and elevated latency overall.

Attached a CSV with a traffic sample and timestamps. Our SREs report repeated client retries hitting your front-facing endpoint which appears to be bouncing requests. We need visibility into any rate-limiter or routing changes on Redwood side — this is causing live revenue impact.

Can someone please confirm receipt and estimated time to first update?

Thanks,
Liam

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike of 503/504 + 429s across EU/APAC — urgent

Summary of initial triage (network + telemetry):
- Observed 503/504 spike starting 08:43:20 UTC concentrated on two front pools in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.
- Token request latencies jumped (p50 -> 450ms, p95 -> 1.6s).
- A large number of concurrent retries from NovusPay user-agents contributed to queue pressure.
- No backend OOMs, but significant queueing at proxy workers.

Immediate mitigations executed:
1) Throttled aggressive retry policy at the front-facing gateway for NovusPay prefix. (temporary)
2) Diverted 15% of NovusPay traffic to a warmed fallback pool in eu-west-2.
3) Increased worker concurrency on the affected pools by +25%.

Remaining actions (in progress):
- Grace: validate whether a config rollout touched the rate-limiter or token bucket windows between 07:50-08:30 UTC.
- Jonas: pull full access logs for the two pools and correlate client retry patterns.
- Messaging: prepare a customer update to confirm actions and ETA.

Marcus

Subject: Re: Spike of 503/504 + 429s across EU/APAC — urgent

Quick post-triage update: likely root cause and recommended next steps.

What we think happened (minimally invasive hypothesis):
- A recent deployment to the "frontdoor" handler adjusted the token-bucket refill window (intended to improve fairness). The change was rolled in as part of a config patch at ~07:58 UTC in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.
- That change reduced the effective burst capacity for some high-throughput customers (NovusPay among them), which caused a larger-than-expected number of 429s.
- Clients (NovusPay SDK) interpreted 429s as transient and retried aggressively, amplifying traffic and causing proxy worker queues to fill -> some requests timed out and surfaced as 503/504.

Recommended durable mitigations:
- Revert the token-bucket refill window change for the next patch in EU/APAC pools (rollback already staged).
- Implement a temporary per-tenant throttle-exemption for NovusPay while we stabilize (rate-limiter delta).
- Add a short-term circuit breaker that converts downstream retries into queued, delayed requests rather than immediate retries (to avoid retry amplification).

We are executing the staged rollback now. Will confirm when the rollout is complete and metrics have recovered.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike of 503/504 + 429s across EU/APAC — update and next steps

Hi Liam — follow-up from our side with the actions taken and next-step plan.

What we did (summary):
- Identified the recent token-bucket refill-window change as the primary trigger. We rolled back that config in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 starting 10:15 UTC; rollout completed 10:47 UTC.
- Temporarily relaxed per-tenant burst limits for NovusPay and routed critical traffic to warmed fallback pools; concurrency increased on the affected pools.
- Implemented a short-term gateway-level backoff to prevent immediate retry amplification (we converted aggressive retries into a short, queued delay at ingress).

Observed results:
- Error rates fell from ~12% to <1.5% within ~30 minutes of the rollback and mitigations.
- Tokenization latency p95 returned to baseline (~220ms).

Next steps (we'll coordinate with your SREs):
1) Joint post-incident review with NovusPay SREs to adjust client-side retry policies (we have recommended exponential backoff with jitter and a max retry cap).
2) Add a temporary per-tenant telemetry dashboard so we can alert earlier on token-bucket saturation.
3) Provide a one-time goodwill credit; we are ready to discuss quantum and agreement path (I'll coordinate with finance).

Attached is a short slide summarizing the timeline and mitigations, plus the traffic sample you shared. Let me know if you'd like a call; Marcus and Grace can join.

Apologies again for the interruption — we take this seriously and want to prevent repeat events.

Best,
